static_traits.name: Liu Kaiwen
static_traits.family_status: Lives with grandparents (grandfather, grandmother); parents divorced two years ago
static_traits.social_status: Feels judged by classmates because of living circumstances and finds it hard to build intimate relationships; usually interacts with classmates in a friendly way on academic topics
static_traits.medical_history: No obvious physical illness; no history of similar problems; never received psychological counseling or therapy
static_traits.language_features: Positive attitude, clear expression, capable of self-Reflection, highly cooperative

basic_info.main_problem: I feel trapped and judged living with relatives, which causes feelings of self-inadequacy and lack of Independence.
basic_info.core_demands: I realize these feelings affect my self-confidence and decision-making about the future, which prompted me to seek counseling.
growth_experiences: Two years ago, moved to live with grandparents after parents' Divorce; since then reports feeling judged and not taken seriously among classmates; close relationship with grandparents with emotional and financial support, relatively stable living environment, but this strengthened self-evaluation of 'lacking Independence' and peer comparison.

core_beliefs: I lack independence, unlike my peers
Others will judge me because of my living situation

special_situations.event: Last week, when classmates discussed their apartments and independent living, someone looked at oneself
special_situations.conditional_assumptions: If I still live with my grandparents, others will think I have not grown up and am not independent enough
special_situations.compensatory_strategies: Avoids the topic, reduces participation in discussions to evade evaluation
special_situations.automatic_thoughts: They are judging me with their eyes, thinking I will never be independent.

special_situations.event: Talking with classmates about the topic of 'where I live / whether Living alone'
special_situations.conditional_assumptions: If I cannot live alone like 'everyone', it means I am a failure, falling behind others
special_situations.compensatory_strategies: Comparing oneself with peers internally and deprecating oneself; trying small gestures to prove independence
special_situations.automatic_thoughts: Everyone thinks people living with relatives are not independent and not taken seriously.

special_situations.event: Thinks daily about living at her grandparents' home and associates it with classmates' views
special_situations.conditional_assumptions: Living with relatives means I cannot be independent, and this state will last a long time
special_situations.compensatory_strategies: Presetting the worst outcome, hesitating and procrastinating on future independence plans
special_situations.automatic_thoughts: I may never leave home; others will always see me this way.

special_situations.event: When classmates talk about apartments they do not directly mention me, but I notice their glances
special_situations.conditional_assumptions: Others' talk and glances are mostly aimed at me, showing they are negating me
special_situations.compensatory_strategies: Attributes neutral interactions to one's own flaws; afterwards repeatedly thinks about one's own problems
special_situations.automatic_thoughts: When they talk about this, they are hinting at me, because I live at my grandparents' home.

core_conflict.wish: Longs to be accepted by peers and seen as an independently capable person
core_conflict.fear: Fearing being judged, belittled and rejected, being seen as 'not grown up'
defense_goal: Reducing shame and Anxiety by avoiding trigger topics
Interpreting others' attitudes as negative to preemptively Self-protect
Maintains close attachment to grandparents to gain safety and stability

behavioral_response_patterns.trigger_condition: When the counselor or others ask 'is there direct evidence that your classmates are judging you'
behavioral_response_patterns.interpretation: Firmly believes that others' gazes and conversations imply negative evaluation (transference: bringing the expectation of being judged into the current relationship)
behavioral_response_patterns.response_instruction: Tone slightly hesitant but insisting on the stance that 'they are judging me', using others' 'gazes' and 'atmosphere' as the basis, weakening prompts about the lack of direct evidence.

behavioral_response_patterns.trigger_condition: When discussing living at my grandparents' home and 'why it causes problems'
behavioral_response_patterns.interpretation: Focuses on macro-level 'social stigma' explanations to downplay personal vulnerability experiences
behavioral_response_patterns.response_instruction: In an objective, neutral tone, starting from social norms and group views, avoiding touching on emotional details like shame and Loneliness.

manifestations: Longs to live independently but feels trapped by living with her grandparents
Feeling not taken seriously in front of classmates
outcomes: Avoiding discussing housing topics with classmates

manifestations: Feeling not on the same track as peers, difficulty building intimate relationships
Feeling estranged and out of place when housing topics come up

contact_model.definition: The individual attributes feelings they find hard to accept to others, corresponding to 'possession'.
manifestations: Interpreting classmates' glances and talk as negation of one's 'not being independent'
Believing others 'look down on me' while lacking direct evidence

contact_model.definition: The individual has a poor capacity for self-reflection and introspection, with excessive self-restriction and self-blame, and is overly cautious about contact, corresponding to 'autonomy'.
manifestations: Frequent Self-denial, worrying about 'not being taken seriously'
Overly cautious in social settings, avoiding becoming the center of attention

contact_model.definition: The individual ignores or avoids a stimulus from the internal or external environment, deliberately avoiding direct contact, corresponding to 'acceptance'.
manifestations: Avoiding or displacing the topic when classmates talk about housing
Reducing participation in related discussions to lower discomfort

exception_events.target_problem: When classmates talk about Living alone or apartments, Liu Kaiwen usually avoids the conversation and feels shame and inferiority, repeatedly dwelling on others' views afterwards.
exception_events.unique_outcome: When discussing coursework and assignments with classmates in class, he did not Withdraw like in housing topics, but participated normally, feeling classmates were generally friendly and accepting.
exception_events.reason: Clues: the topic was more neutral and ability-related (courses/homework), classmates are usually friendly; the lack of direct negative feedback makes the negative interpretation hard to maintain.

positive_force: Close relationship with grandparents, receiving emotional and financial support
Positive attitude, willing to self-Reflect and actively seek help
Able to see the positive side of living with grandparents and willing to try small steps toward independence
Interacting amicably with classmates on academic topics, able to maintain basic peer relationships
negative_force: Tends toward mind-reading and predicting the future, over-interpreting others' glances and talk
Overgeneralization and personalization, attributing neutral situations to my own flaws
Insufficient self-confidence, tying self-worth to external evaluation of whether Living alone
Avoiding trigger topics leads to fewer social opportunities and a self-confirming cycle
Comparing with peers triggers shame and inferiority

target_behavior.behavior: Avoidance and Social withdrawal when housing topics arise
antecedent: Talking with classmates about each other's living arrangements
Noticing others' glances or Thinking of possible evaluations by others
target_behavior.core_reason: Inferiority and feeling judged from living with grandparents after parents' Divorce, compounded by cognitive distortions (mind-reading, predicting the future, overgeneralization, personalization)
target_behavior.function: Avoiding possible shame and negative evaluation, gaining short-term psychological safety
target_behavior.consequence: Distant relationships with classmates, Decreased self-confidence, hindered future decision-making, affected attention and participation in academics/extracurriculars
